authors: M. Ehsan Karim
title: Cross-Fitted Survey-Weighted TMLE with Design-Based Variance for Causal Machine Learning
what_it_holds: Cross-fitting at the PSU level (whole PSUs assigned to V folds, balanced within strata) for survey-weighted TMLE under stratified multistage designs. Variance is ultimate-cluster Taylor linearization with PSU as replication unit scaled by m_h/(m_h-1), with no explicit FPC in Eq. 3 (FPC treatment is deferred to Web Appendix A and F, which I did not see). Wald statistics are referred to a t distribution with survey df = PSUs minus strata (50 df in both simulation designs, 60 PSUs in 10 strata and 100 PSUs in 50 strata). Cross-fitted coverage in the 2-PSU-per-stratum design is 0.916, which the paper calls the familiar finite-sample cost of sample splitting; SE/SD about 1.45 at the under-smoothed learner. It is causal TMLE, not PPI, and the smallest design has 60 PSUs. Read through an extraction of the html, so details outside Sections 3 to 5 were not seen.

authors: Pranav Mani, Peng Xu, Zachary C. Lipton, Michael Oberst
title: No Free Lunch: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Exact finite-sample variance of cross-fit PPI++ for mean estimation under iid sampling with sample splitting. Theorem 4.1 (Eq. 2) gives four terms: classical variance, efficiency gain from the pseudo-label covariance, an efficiency loss from estimating lambda (third term), and a cross-term between folds (fourth term, order 1/n^2). Gaussian threshold for improvement over labels only is |rho| > (n/2-2)^(-1/2) for cross-fit and 1/sqrt(n-2) without splitting. A plug-in variance that treats lambda as fixed is always optimistic (Prop 4.6) and single-sample PPI++ is biased (Prop 4.5). Estimated-lambda inflation is O(1/n), so asymptotic analyses miss it. No clusters and no finite-population results (only one Gaussian result with finite N), so it covers the estimated-lambda variance cost but not the fpc structure in C1. Read through a pdf extraction.

authors: Xin Lu, Lei Shi, Hanzhong Liu, Peng Ding
title: Conditional cross-fitting for unbiased machine-learning-assisted covariate adjustment in randomized experiments
what_it_holds: Design-based (randomization-only) cross-fitting for ATE in Bernoulli, completely randomized and stratified experiments. Algorithm 1 randomly splits units into two disjoint subsets with split-specific inverse-probability weights, fits prediction functions on one subset and estimates on the other, and combines the two with weights N_q/N. Estimator is unbiased conditional on the split. The text I could see writes the oracle variance as the expected within-subsample variances with no between-split term. Variance estimator is a generic conservative Neyman-type estimator applied to cross-fitted residuals (CRE case uses N1(N1-1) and N0(N0-1) denominators). No FPC discussion, no t reference, no clusters, smallest simulation N is about 316. Part of Section 5 text was truncated in the extraction, so the absence of an fpc-free term is not fully confirmed.

authors: Xinhe Wang, Ben B. Hansen
title: Robust Design-Based Estimation and Inference for Stratified Randomized Trials with Varying Cluster Sizes
what_it_holds: Design-based inference in stratified cluster-randomized trials with varying cluster sizes. Proposes a Hajek (ratio) estimator and a design-based variance estimator that is asymptotically conservative for any number of strata, including strata with one treated or one control unit. Gives a score-based test (Section 4.3) that improves coverage over Wald when the number of clusters is moderate. The test uses normal critical values with no t or df, and the paper notes that Wald with an n-2 df adjustment still under-covers in small samples. No FPC is used. Simulations with 10 or 50 strata of size 2 to 50. Covariate adjustment is plug-in with no cross-fitting.

authors: Alberto Abadie, Susan Athey, Guido W. Imbens, Jeffrey M. Wooldridge

Proposes new variance estimators for intermediate cases where conventional cluster-robust errors are too large and heteroskedasticity-robust errors too small. This is the design-based clustering reference named in the seed list. The companion Econometrica 2020 paper (sampling-based vs design-based uncertainty) was not looked up.

authors: Tijana Zrnic, Emmanuel J. Candes
title: Cross-Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Cross-PPI. K labelled folds, a model f^(j) trained on all folds except fold j, unlabeled points scored by all K models, and a debiasing term from out-of-fold residuals (Eq. 4). Variance is estimated by bootstrap (Sec. 6, B = 30). All theory is asymptotic, iid, K fixed, with stability conditions (Assumption 1 and 2) to handle dependence among fold models. No finite-population theory, no FPC, no t reference, no clusters. Does not use a fold-specific tuning coefficient lambda.

authors: Edward Wu, Johann A. Gagnon-Bartsch
title: The LOOP Estimator: Adjusting for Covariates in Randomized Experiments
venue_or_arxiv: Evaluation Review 42(4):458-488 (2018) per search-result URL [verify]; arXiv:1708.01229
what_it_holds: [from abstract only] Leave-one-out potential outcomes estimator. Each unit is removed in turn, its treated and control outcomes are predicted by any algorithm such as a random forest, and results are aggregated. Unbiased under the Neyman-Rubin model (randomization is the only randomness) and generally at least as precise as the unadjusted estimator. A design-based leave-one-out relative of cross-fitting, with variance under complete randomization rather than under sampling of clusters.

authors: Stefan Wager, Wenfei Du, Jonathan Taylor, Robert J. Tibshirani
title: High-dimensional regression adjustments in randomized experiments
venue_or_arxiv: PNAS (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1614732113 per arXiv page; volume and pages [verify]); arXiv:1607.06801
what_it_holds: Cross-estimation. Units split into K folds (K = 5 or 10), regression adjustments for fold k fit on the other folds, fold estimates averaged with weights n_k/n. Theorem 4 gives finite-sample unbiasedness conditional on covariates, without assumptions on the regression. Asymptotic variance (Eq. 19) and interval (Eq. 20 to 21) use the sum of fold-level variances weighted by (n_k/n)^2 with normal quantiles. The framework is iid with Neyman-Rubin potential outcomes, so no finite-population correction, no between-fold variance term, no clusters.

authors: M. Dagdoug and D. Haziza
title: Machine learning methods for finite population parameter estimation in survey sampling
what_it_holds: Review of ML in survey inference. Section 3.3 gives a cross-fitted model-assisted estimator under Poisson sampling with honest residuals in a Horvitz-Thompson-type variance estimator. Section 3.4 treats K = 2 cross-fitting under other designs and gives a design-unbiased version using conditional inclusion probabilities, with variance estimation delegated to An et al. (2026b). Section 4.3 (cross-fitted AIPW for item nonresponse) says 'assuming the sampling fraction n/N is negligible' and drops the second variance term. Cluster or PSU sampling is not discussed. Shows the field explicitly sets the sampling fraction aside for cross-fitted estimators.
